findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the Certified Food Manager Certificate (CFM) on file to have expired in March of last year. The person in charge (PIC) stated that they have not retaken the test since then. Inspector provided PIC with a handout on accredited institutes through which they may retake the exam. A CFM must be on site at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM helps to oversee proper food handling and cold holding temperatures to ensure facility is in compliance with safe food handling and preparation. Retake the test by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 
During today’s visit inspectors observed multiple items in the hand sink. PIC was made aware and Items were removed. Ensure that the hand sink is available for hand washing at all times. 

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mouse dropping next to a bag of wheat flour in the facility’s dry storage area. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) cleaned the area immediately. Ensure the facility is cleaned on a routine basis to eliminate conditions for pest harborage.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) 
Multiple cardboard boxes of food items were observed store directly on the floor in different areas in the facility. PIC was informed. PIC assured inspectors that the boxes will be removed from the floor. Ensure that food items stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect them from form splash, dust, or other contamination.

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
6-101.11(A)
Inspectors observed ice accumulation in multiple Chest sliding freezer. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated Ice accumulation will be clean. Ensure that Ice is cleaned to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated inspected that training will be done soon. Ensure all workers who handle or prepare food have and maintain their Food Handler’s Certificate every 3 years. Food Handler’s must have a certificate on file within 30 days of hire. Ensure these documents are available upon request during future inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The PIC was unable to produce signed Employee Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. The inspector provided the PIC with a blank copy of Sangamon County Department of Public Health’s Employee Reporting Agreement. The inspector will return on 10/16/25 to ensure all employees have signed and read the agreement. Ensure these documents are kept on file to be produced during inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple items (pork belly, Mackerel, Tilapia) to have torn packaging, or be outside of their packaging in the sliding chest coolers & freezers. CORRECTED- items were re-wrapped. Ensure all temperature control for safety (TCS) food items that are packaged on site retain their seal to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the sliding chest cooler in front of the food prep area to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the PIC added an ambient thermometer to the cooling unit. Ensure all cooling units contain an ambient thermometer to measure the temperature at the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility ensure all cooling units are working properly to hold items at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: 1) Inspectors observed mouse droppings on the floor and between boxes in the back dry storage area (shipping container). 
2) Inspector also observed a dead bug on a noodle package on the top shelf of the open air cooler. CORRECTED- this item was removed from service by the PIC.

The facility uses Sonny Adams for Pest Control once monthly. Droppings should be cleaned up, but large pallets of food will need to be moved to properly clean. Contact pest control operator, and monitor the area for evidence of pest after clean up, and check shipments for pests during delivery.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a significant amount of brown rice being stored in a cardboard box, with an open top in the back dry storage area. Foods in dry storage should be completely covered in a food-grade package or container to prevent the contamination of food. This storage method also may attract pests (see violation #38). Ensure foods are protected from contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hot water is not available at the prep area handwashing sink. Ensure hot water is available at all handwashing sinks. The valve was turned-off at the start of the inspection. See that hot water is always available. A new hot water heater was just installed and hot water was able to be supplied during the inspection. 
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Quail eggs were observed in a double door cooler above kimchi and other packaged items. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged to keep quail eggs below packaged foods. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st  REPEAT: No ambient thermometer is present in the 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC added a thermometer to the cooler. 
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Repackaged frozen meats observed in two chest freezers without appropriate labeling. The facility has been able to properly label multiple foods, there remains some whole, intact fish that need proper cooking instructions (the common name is indicated on the freezer holding the foods. See that cooking instructions are available either on the packaging OR simply print a label to affix to the front of the freezer.  

3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: The facility is receiving regular pest control treatment from Sonny Adams, service occurred on November 14. There are still a very small number of mouse droppings observed in the far back storage area. Droppings are minimal and may be easily cleaned BUT pallets of bulk foods will need to be moved in-order to properly clean. Continue to provide regular PCO service and monitor and clean when activity is observed.  No damaged packaging is observed. 

The facility will be given thirty days to inspect to allow ample time for proper cleaning. 
PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: There is no bleach available within the store. The facility does minimal processing and does not immediately need the sanitizer. See that bleach is provided and that the available test strips are used to determine the proper concentration (100-200ppm).

(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There is pressed wood shelving over the triple sink that is unsealed. Properly seal/paint the shelves so the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Also, a couple of the reach-in freezers are observed to have significant ice accumulation. Defrost the freezers so they are able to be easily cleaned. 
Also, there is cardboard being used on the top of a roll cart adjacent to the wrapping station. See that the cardboard is removed and replaced with a cleanable surfaces (think plastic sheet). The cardboard is protecting over single-service items. The cardboard is starting to show signs of wear and should be replaced with a suitable alternative.  

(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
